source: Jiang et al. (2026) Synapse: Empowering LLM Agents with Episodic-Semantic Memory via Spreading Activation
finding: Re-read in full this session (HTML). Main table and ablation numbers match the earlier notes. SYNAPSE leads LoCoMo with GPT-4o-mini, but the margin over Zep is small.
numbers: Table 1, weighted F1 over four non-adversarial categories: Synapse 40.5, Zep 39.7, MemoryOS 38.0, LangMem 34.3, AriGraph 33.7, A-Mem 33.3. Paired t-test p<.05 on N=500 instances. Single-hop: Synapse 48.9, Zep 48.0, A-Mem 44.7. Ablation (Table 3): no node decay avg 30.7 (temporal 50.1 to 14.2); no fan effect avg 36.1 (open-domain 25.9 to 16.8, multi-hop 35.7 to 30.2); no activation dynamics avg 30.5; vectors only 25.2.
limits: One benchmark (LoCoMo), the authors' own code, LLM-judged secondary metrics. Margin over Zep is 0.8 F1.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 partly closed: the numbers are real. The paper ablates whole mechanisms, not an ACT-R base-level term.

source: Jiang et al. (2026) Synapse, Appendix F cross-backbone results (Table 12)
finding: The SYNAPSE lead repeats on other backbones, but only by the same authors and on the same benchmark.
numbers: Average F1: GPT-4o: Synapse 43.4, A-Mem 36.1, MemGPT 32.0, LoCoMo full-context 29.5. Qwen-3b: Synapse 36.6, MemoryOS 22.1, A-Mem 16.2. Qwen-1.5b: A-Mem 20.4 (Synapse row not read). On GPT-4o, full-context LoCoMo beats Synapse on single-hop (61.6 vs 46.5).
limits: Same dataset, same group. Not an independent replication. No benchmark without a newer-is-right bias.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: backbone part supported. Benchmark part still open.

source: Jiang et al. (2026) Synapse, Appendix C hyperparameter sensitivity (Table 6)
finding: Results are fairly flat around the defaults. Propagation depth matters most. The decay parameter has a visible but small effect.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini, LoCoMo avg F1 (temporal F1): delta 0.3 = 40.0 (51.2); delta 0.5 default = 40.5 (50.1); delta 0.7 = 38.1 (46.5). Spreading S 0.6/0.8/1.0 = 38.3/40.5/38.8. Propagation T 2/3/4 = 37.7/40.5/40.1.
limits: Defaults appear picked on the same test set. Delta here is a per-step leak, not a time constant.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: a 0.3 to 0.7 sweep of the decay-like term costs at most 2.4 avg F1 here. Weak sensitivity, not none.

source: Jiang et al. (2026) Synapse, equation 2 and implementation details
finding: Correction. SYNAPSE node decay is a per-step leak on graph activation, (1-delta)*a, with delta=0.5 over T=3 propagation steps. Time enters only through temporal edge weights exp(-rho*|tau_i - tau_j|), rho=0.01. There is no use count and no time-since-last-use term.
numbers: Hybrid retrieval weights 0.5 semantic, 0.3 activation, 0.2 structural. About 814 tokens per query vs 16,910 for full context. Low-similarity subsets (cos below 0.3): Synapse falls 7.4%, A-Mem falls 56.3%. Authors list Cold Start and Cognitive Tunneling as failure modes.
limits: The reading of the equations is mine, from the HTML text. The ablation that hurts temporal questions removes this leak, so it shows value of time-aware spreading on LoCoMo, not of base-level learning.
agent_relevance: K10 should not be cited as support for ACT-R base-level decay. It supports fan dilution and a time-aware graph on a temporal benchmark.

source: Honda, Fujita, Zempo & Fukushima (2025) Human-Like Remembering and Forgetting in LLM Agents: An ACT-R-Inspired Memory Architecture (HAI '25)
finding: The paper exists (ACM HAI 2025, DOI 10.1145/3765766.3765803, dated 2025-11-10). Abstract only: dialogue agent with ACT-R-style activation made of temporal decay, semantic similarity and probabilistic noise.
numbers: No numbers in the abstract. It claims simulations reproduce reinforcement through repeated topics and stochastic retrieval variability, and that optimal parameters were found for balancing contextual sensitivity and stability.
limits: Abstract read via OpenAlex. ACM full text returned 403. No baseline, benchmark or accuracy known. It is a simulation, not a comparison with Park.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 closed on existence, open on results. Cite no effect size from it.

source: Hou et al. (2024) 'My agent understands me better' (arXiv 2404.00573), Task 0 tables
finding: Task 0 (user says they will go to a concert next Thursday, which breaks the usual Thursday pattern) was failed by both models, in opposite ways.
numbers: Model 1 (recall-count decay): University 0.850 vs Home 0.830, Library 0.836, Restaurant 0.836, so it picked the habitual event. Model 2 (Park-style): Restaurant (most recent, 55,800 s) scored 1.620 vs University 1.489, so recency picked the one-off. Elapsed times 55,800 to 434,700 s. Overall across tasks t=-5.687, p=0.000299.
limits: 10 author-built tasks. Clock is elapsed wall seconds. Task 0 is one item, so this shows direction of failure only.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: frequency hurts on the exception, and so does recency. Neither term alone covers it. A goal or gist fit term is needed.

source: Rana et al. (2026) OBLIVION: Self-Adaptive Agentic Memory Control through Decay-Driven Activation (v3)
finding: Re-read. Retention is R=exp(-n/S) with S=(utility+frequency+eps)*T, where n is turns since the cluster was last reinforced. Items are not deleted but can be evicted from the working buffer. There is no ablation of decay on versus decay off.
numbers: LongMemEval S, GPT-4.1-mini: 90.60 vs direct baseline 89.00. Hierarchy ablation (Table 3): L2 only 86.40, L2+L3 89.60, all layers 90.60 (tokens/query 13,124 vs 23,987 for L3 alone). GoodAILTM 2K Table 16, buffer 60: T=1 8.41, T=3 6.97, T=5 6.69, T=10 7.78, T=20 6.88, T=50 6.55. Buffer 90: 6.74, 7.16, 6.74, 7.46, 7.41, 7.16.
limits: Text says T=10 is best, but at buffer 60 the table shows T=1 highest. Scores are non-monotone, so noise is the size of the T effect. Three runs averaged, no CI. The 1.6 point gain is not tied to decay.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open: no rank-versus-delete test. Gap 2: a turn-count clock. Gap 10: T is task- and buffer-dependent and noisy.

source: Wei et al. (2026) FadeMem: Biologically-Inspired Forgetting for Efficient Agent Memory (v2)
finding: FadeMem uses a stretched exponential, v(t)=v0*exp(-lambda*dt^beta), with beta 0.8 for long-term and 1.2 for short-term layers, plus a saturating frequency term f/(1+f) in importance. Its ablations remove modules, not the frequency term or the decay form.
numbers: Ablation on LoCoMo: no dual layer, multi-hop F1 29.43 to 19.45 (-33.9%); no fusion, to 13.63 (-53.7%). Importance = alpha*relevance + beta*f/(1+f) + gamma*exp(-delta*dt). Raw count is replaced by a time-decayed access rate.
limits: beta values are set by hand, not fitted. Single benchmark. No power-law arm.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 3: a frequency term exists in a design but nobody isolated it. Gap 3 stays open.

source: Lai (2026) CAMeR: Keyword-Gated Hybrid Activation for Adaptive Memory Retention in LLM Agents (v1)
finding: The only agent-memory benchmark found that is built to test use history: 76 memories, 8 topic clusters, 100 query rounds, query counts from 37 for high-frequency clusters down to 0 for controls. It scores memory weights, not answer accuracy.
numbers: Decay 0.99 per round, reinforcement +0.2, long-term decay 0.995. Retention gap between frequent and never-used memories: keyword-gated 0.039 vs embedding-only 0.024 (1.6x). Time-driven baselines (Oblivion, SuperLocalMemory) fall to near zero over 100 rounds. Top-5 retrieval 39k vs 231k cumulative tokens (83.2% saved). Eight ablations: the keyword gate matters, learnable decay does not at this scale.
limits: Single author, synthetic, 76 memories, English only, no end-task accuracy. Absolute gaps are small.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: a seed for the smallest benchmark. Gap 2: the clock is the query round. Gap 7: pure time-driven decay collapses, use-driven reinforcement keeps weights alive.

source: Averell & Heathcote (2011) The form of the forgetting curve and the fate of memories (J Math Psychol 55:25-35)
finding: Hierarchical Bayesian fit of forgetting curves from 1 min to 28 days. An exponential fit individual curves best. Bayesian model selection favoured a power function. Both supported above-zero asymptote.
numbers: Cued recall and stem completion, 1 min to 28 days, more observations per interval per participant than earlier work. N and fit statistics not read.
limits: Abstract only (figshare record). Full text paywalled. The split between individual-level and Bayesian conclusions is the point: form depends on the analysis.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: even the best human study gives no clean winner, so test the decay form on the agent's own data. Do not claim power law is proven.

source: Hu et al. (2025) Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions (MemoryAgentBench)
finding: Benchmark with four competencies: accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, selective forgetting (FactConsolidation, overwrite of old facts). None varies how often an item was used.
numbers: Selective forgetting: all methods reach at most 28% on multi-hop; only long-context agents do fairly on single-hop. Long-context models best on TTL and LRU. LongMemEval reformulated to 5 dialogues of about 355K tokens with 300 questions.
limits: Tests recency of a fact (overwrite), not frequency or spacing.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: not a use-history test, but it can host the exception side (new fact replaces habit). Add a frequency manipulation.

source: Anon. (2026) Retrieval Beats Cheap Structured Memory: A Cost-Retention Study (Preprints 202608.1369)
finding: Abstract only. Seven memory strategies on LoCoMo and LongMemEval. Plain BM25 retrieval holds retention at 98% fewer tokens. No decay or recency scheme is among the strategies.
numbers: LoCoMo n=160: BM25 39.4% vs full context 30.6% (sign test p=0.09, not significant). LongMemEval knowledge-update n=72: slots 37.5% vs retrieval 73.6%. Short-history categories n=254: full context leads BM25 by 10.2 points (p=0.004).
limits: Abstract only, non-peer-reviewed preprint, small n.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: plain retrieval at equal tokens is a hard baseline, and gains of 1 to 3 points need hundreds of items to show.

source: Rocchi (2026) Does Memory Credit Travel? Paired Factorial Audits of LLM-Agent Memory (SSRN 7160321)
finding: Abstract only. On ALFWorld, most successes that follow a retrieved memory are not caused by it. Crediting a memory for being retrieved gives mostly passenger credit.
numbers: 576 episodes, 48 target configurations, Qwen3-32B and Mistral Small 3.1-24B. Bank-only success already 166/192 (86.5%). Of 169 joint successes a retrieval ledger would credit, 10 were marginal helps (5.9% precision) and 159 passenger. Stress subset: passenger credit 94.7 to 100%.
limits: Abstract only. One environment. The controller comparison was non-informative, as the authors say.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: if base-level activation counts every retrieval as a use, it reinforces passengers. Count a use only when the answer depends on the memory.

source: Maurya (2026) Beyond the Single Forgetting Curve: typologically-extended Wickelgren function (SSRN 6933638)
finding: Abstract only. Theory, simulation and a preregistered plan; no human results. Uses the Wickelgren power law R=lambda*(1+beta*t)^-psi with error-type-specific parameters.
numbers: 500-replication simulation, n=90, time points 0, 2, 7, 14 days. No participant data.
limits: No empirical result. Not evidence for any form.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: listed so it is not mistaken for a test of power versus exponential.

source: Synthesis of clock choice across LLM-memory papers read this session (Park 2023, Hou 2024, OBLIVION, CAMeR, SYNAPSE)
finding: Each paper picked a different clock and none compared clocks. Park: game hours since last retrieval, 0.995 per hour. Hou: elapsed wall seconds. OBLIVION: turns since last reinforcement. CAMeR: query rounds, 0.99 per round. SYNAPSE: timestamp gaps on edges (rho=0.01) plus a per-step leak.
numbers: No clock ablation in any of the five. CAMeR 0.99^100 = 0.366. OBLIVION T from 1 to 50 spans fast to flat curves.
limits: A missing comparison cannot be proven by search alone, and search tools were rate limited this session (arXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex search, WebSearch).
agent_relevance: Gap 2 stays open. Cheapest test: one memory store scored with three clocks on the same replay.
